Header: Eutetranychus orientalis (Klein) and Panonychus citri (McGregor) Purple mite or citrus red mite

Prevention: Avoid planting citrus next to previously infested fields.
Practice proper field hygiene by maintaining weed free fields.
Protect natural enemies such as spiders, dragonflies, ladybird beetles, predatory wasps and parasitic wasps through conservation of patches of natural vegetation.
Monitoring: Check on both sides of the leaves for small red, brown or creamy eight legged pests.
Inspect leaves for webing and/or leaf curling.
Inspect leaves for browning and/or wilting during extreme dry conditions.
Inspect trees for fruit and leaf drop in early attacks especially if moisture is low in the soil
Start control when 8-10 mites per leaf are observed
Direct Control (Non-chemical): In case of low levels of infestation, wash off the mites with a jet of running water and remove the affected leaves.
Remove and destroy by burning or burying crop residues immediately after harvest.
Nimbecidine at 5ml/L of water to reduce the populations.
PHYTOTECH Apply 50-100 mites per m2 or 500,000-1 million mites per hectare.
Rates will be dependent on estimated number of spider mites by way of scouting.
P. persimilis to 5 mites depending on the risk of assessment)
Direct Control (Chemical): Abamectin 50g/L (Twigamectin 18EC at the rate of 10mls/20L of water
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
Apply at first symptoms according to the threshold.
Product unlikely to present hazard under conditions of normal use.
No more than 1 spray during flowering.
Toxic to bees and aquatic organisms
